definitions.gloss: to abandon, to forsake, to desert
definitions.explanation: To give up on someone or something and leave them without help or care. Carries a strong emotional connotation of betrayal or cold-heartedness.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}を{見捨|みす}てるわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I can't just abandon my friend.

examples.japanese: {困|こま}っている{人|ひと}を{見捨|みす}てないでほしい。
examples.english: Please don't turn your back on people in trouble.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}が{倒産|とうさん}しそうになると、{社員|しゃいん}たちは{次々|つぎつぎ}と{会社|かいしゃ}を{見捨|みす}てて{辞|や}めていった。
examples.english: When the company was on the verge of bankruptcy, the employees deserted one after another.

notes:
USAGE:
{見捨|みす}てる is a compound verb from {見|み} (see) and {捨|す}てる (to throw away). It implies a deliberate decision to stop caring about or helping someone. The phrase {見捨|みす}てるわけにはいかない (I can't just abandon...) is very common and expresses moral obligation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見捨|みす}てるわけにはいかない: can't just abandon
- {見捨|みす}てられる: to be abandoned/forsaken (passive)
- {見捨|みす}てないで: don't abandon me/us
- {神|かみ}に{見捨|みす}てられる: to be forsaken by God
